summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for October 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: It is like a monthly count of how many cars used each road, written down so people can see which roads are busy.

subtitle: A monthly table of how many packets each ARPANET Host sent in October 1973.

tldr.problem: The network operators wanted to record how much traffic each Host put onto the network.
tldr.mechanism: The memo attaches a table of packets output per Host for October 1973, split into internode and intranode counts, with totals and an average daily internode figure.
tldr.outcome: It is a data report, not a protocol. The table ends with network totals and a packets-per-message ratio for internode traffic.

today: This is a one-off data report that updates RFC 579. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown and shows no later RFC replacing it.

sections.title: A Traffic Report
sections.content:
A. McKenzie of BBN-NET attaches the Host traffic statistics for October 1973. The cover note is a single sentence, and the RFC updates RFC 579, the earlier traffic report.

The attachment is titled Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). It lists each site and each of its numbered Hosts, such as UCLA HOST 0, SRI HOST 0 or ISI HOST 1.
sections.plainLanguage: The note says here are the numbers for last month, and then hands over a long list of counts.

sections.title: Reading the Table
sections.content:
Each row gives inter-node packets, intra-node packets and a total. A site with several Hosts also gets a subtotal line, plus an average daily internode figure and the number of days counted.

Most sites show 31 days. A few differ, such as LLL with 29 and WRPAT with 28. SDC, ABER and LBL are listed as having had no traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: For each computer there are two counts: messages that stayed at its own spot and messages sent to other spots. The table adds them up.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
The final lines give totals of 93524810 internode packets and 23672870 intranode packets. The daily averages are 3016929 and 763641, and the average per node-day is 73874 and 18699.

The last line gives a packets-per-message ratio for internode traffic of 1.09. In the data, ISI HOST 1 has the largest single internode figure at 12350080.
sections.plainLanguage: At the bottom there is a grand total, which shows how busy the whole network was that month.

references.text: RFC 579, the earlier traffic statistics report that this one updates.
